paths.description: Homepage listing and search entry point; represents the primary content-discovery template. Conditions: desktop, 360 px narrow viewport, light/dark theme, reduced motion, forced colors, keyboard focus, no-JS crawler, performance/network/memory.
Category index; represents taxonomy/list navigation and repeated card-grid template.
Representative video detail page; covers title, player gate, related content, engagement, and premium promotion.
Primary account flow through consent rejection, provider choice, email form reveal, and invalid empty submit. No account was created.
Deliberately invalid route; represents HTTP/not-found recovery.

Authenticated history/subscriptions, upload, actual account creation, payment, cancellation, and post-age-verification playback were not covered because they require credentials, identity/age verification, payment, or side effects. Distinct public templates were otherwise represented.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference is ignored
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, eight 2-second shimmer animations remained running and no reduced-motion CSS rule was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop skeleton shimmer and other non-essential motion inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: Route changes have no transition treatment
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules across listing, category, signup, and detail destinations, so full-page navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin pages with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long listings provide no scroll-state feedback
findings.evidence: The long homepage and category screenshots show fixed chrome but no progress, shrinking header, or scroll-state cue; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a shrinking sticky header or lightweight scroll progress affordance that respects reduced motion.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the core page on every fresh load
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots of home, category, video, signup, and 404 show a centered cookie panel covering the primary content; the age-verification banner adds a second interruption.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep reject immediately available, remember the choice, and replace the blocking first-load panel with a less intrusive consent surface where lawful.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay lacks dialog semantics
findings.evidence: DOM recon found no <dialog> or role=dialog while the screenshot shows a modal interaction layer, denying assistive technology a reliable modal boundary.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog>, focus management, an accessible name, Escape handling where allowed, and restore focus on close.

findings.summary: The desktop layout is forced into a 360 px viewport
findings.evidence: At viewport 360x800, layout measured 1024 px scroll width and 664 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot shows the left sidebar and clipped content rather than a mobile layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real responsive layout: collapse the sidebar/navigation, remove fixed minimum widths, and verify scrollWidth equals the visual viewport at 320–412 px.

findings.summary: Reusable cards do not adapt at component level
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules, while the narrow screenshot shows desktop-sized navigation/sidebar/card composition clipped into the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reused grids/cards containment and use size container queries to switch card and navigation composition at available inline size.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and some touch targets are too small
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus found outline-style none on sampled links, buttons, and inputs; Lighthouse target-size failed and identified a 20 px-high link.
findings.suggestedFix: Add high-contrast :focus-visible styles and ensure every interactive target has at least 24x24 CSS px of unobscured target area, preferably 44x44.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is outside the good range
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.8 s (score 0.55), though the raw trace on desktop measured 1.56 s. The mobile result misses the 2.5 s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP element, reduce critical CSS/JS, and defer nonessential widgets until after the primary listing is visible.

findings.summary: The initial page ships a large script and dependency footprint
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 139 requests, 1.65 MB transferred, 60 scripts totaling 1.01 MB, three parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets, and a 400 KB index script.
findings.suggestedFix: Split and conditionally load route/widget code, remove unused locale/features from the entry path, and defer third-party widgets until needed.

findings.summary: Accessible names and semantics fail on core controls and lists
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.75 and found an unnamed button, label/content-name mismatches on video links, and invalid list children; the signup probe also found an unnamed submit button.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a stable accessible name matching visible text, keep only li children in ul, and label email controls explicitly.

findings.summary: Important text fails WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found age-banner text at 2.15:1 and 1.75:1, view counts at 3.29:1, and links indistinguishable from surrounding text.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust tokens to at least 4.5:1 for normal text and add a non-colour link cue such as underline.

findings.summary: Focus indication and list structure are not dependable
findings.evidence: Focus probe found none outlines across sampled interactive elements; Lighthouse reported invalid ul children and accessibility-tree issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore :focus-visible outlines, fix list semantics, and verify logical keyboard order across the consent, header, cards, and signup form.

findings.summary: Zoom is disabled and reflow fails
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found user-scalable=no in the runtime viewport meta; the 360 px evidence also shows 664 px horizontal overflow and clipped content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no, permit unrestricted pinch zoom, and make all content reflow without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS px.

findings.summary: Image sizing is structurally weak
findings.evidence: Image audit found 29 of 36 images without width/height, 12 oversized, eight below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and three without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio, serve density-appropriate srcset candidates, and lazy-load below-fold thumbnails.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks social and structured metadata
findings.evidence: Rendered HTML inspection found no Open Graph tags and no JSON-LD on a public media catalogue homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata and schema.org WebSite/Organization metadata; add VideoObject on detail pages.

findings.summary: Browser defenses and cookie flags are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers expose a CSP limited to frame-ancestors, omit X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy, and HSTS is only one day. Cookies audit found settings and x_csrf_token without Secure; settings uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive nonce/hash CSP, nosniff, strict referrer policy, longer HSTS after validation, and Secure/SameSite-appropriate cookie flags.

findings.summary: A large third-party footprint loads before consent
findings.evidence: Fresh-load HAR recorded 115 third-party requests and 1.55 MB from 15 origins, including accounts.google.com and tsyndicate.com, while the consent dialog was still awaiting a choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Block nonessential third-party requests until affirmative consent, proxy or remove unnecessary vendors, and batch first-party analytics.

findings.summary: Authentication offers passwords and federated providers but no passkey path
findings.evidence: Signup walkthrough exposed Google, X, email, and a password field; platform/source probes found no visible WebAuthn or passkey option.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside account recovery, retaining federated/email fallbacks.

findings.summary: Rendered numeric abbreviations are not German-locale aware
findings.evidence: The German UI displays counts such as “2.6M Aufrufe” and “718.9K”, using English decimal points and abbreviations instead of locale-aware German formatting.
findings.suggestedFix: Format counts with Intl.NumberFormat for the active locale and use localized compact notation.

findings.summary: Promotional and consent surfaces compete with core content
findings.evidence: Screenshots show a repeated blocking consent panel, an age-verification banner, premium upsells, and third-party/promotional cards embedded among the primary media grid.
findings.suggestedFix: Clearly label ads/promotions, reduce repeated interruption, preserve equal reject/accept choice, and separate monetisation from organic results.

findings.summary: The email signup field disables autofill
findings.evidence: Signup email probe found email inputs with autocomplete=off while the password correctly uses new-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=email and autocomplete=email (or username as appropriate), remove the duplicate hidden-looking email control, and retain new-password.

findings.summary: Account consent is broad and the submit affordance is not clearly named
findings.evidence: Signup states that personal data will be publicly accessible and used by partners, while the form probe found an unnamed submit button and no granular account-data choices.
findings.suggestedFix: Clarify which profile data becomes public, separate optional partner processing, and give the submit control a visible and accessible action name.

findings.summary: Thumbnail delivery wastes bytes
findings.evidence: Image audit found 12 oversized images, 16 legacy-format detections, missing dimensions on 29 images, and eight below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve right-sized AVIF/WebP srcset candidates, reserve intrinsic size, and lazy-load noncritical thumbnails.

findings.summary: Repeated feed scrolling grows an already large heap
findings.evidence: Heap summary rose from 676,207 nodes / 36.16 MB self size to 743,513 nodes / 39.58 MB after ten bottom/top scroll cycles, a 10.0% node and 9.5% size increase. Separate-load variance lowers confidence, but the retained growth merits investigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat baseline/target/final snapshots in one session with forced GC, bound feed caches, and clean observers/listeners for discarded cards.
